result.title: GesBench: When and Where Do Multimodal Language Models Perceive Social Meaning?
result.summary: Human social perception is incremental: we infer intent before an utterance is complete, revise our interpretation as new cues arrive, and attend to specific facial, gestural, or prosodic signals that shape social meaning. Current multimodal LLM benchmarks largely evaluate final-answer understanding over complete episodes, rewarding post-hoc recognition of social meaning rather than the unfolding perception required for real-time interaction. Drawing on interactionally embedded Gestalt principles of multimodal human communication, we introduce GesBench: a human-grounded benchmark for cue-level social perception in multimodal LLMs. GesBench uses cumulative sub-utterance clips to measure when models form stable interpretations of speaker intention and social affordance, and human gaze-guided corruption to evaluate whether regions attended by humans are functionally important for model judgments. Built from more than 6000 utterance-level clips from scripted and unscripted conversational datasets, GesBench includes human annotations of unfolding judgments and gaze on a representative subset. Across open and closed multimodal models, we find a clear human-model gap: humans form predictive understandings early and revise more often, while models often hedge or repeat across different clips. GesBench shifts social evaluation from whether models eventually recognize meaning to when and where that meaning is formed. Our codes are publicly available at https://anonymous.4open.science/status/GesBench-share-212C.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 GesBench，用累积的子话语片段测量多模态 LLM 何时形成稳定的说话人意图与社会可供性判断，并以人类注视引导的破坏实验检验人关注区域是否对模型判断具有功能作用，从而把社会意义评估从「最终是否识别」转向「何时、何处形成」。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「何时形成稳定解释」与注视引导破坏所考察的视觉证据因果作用，可为 LVR 中视觉证据筛选、动态计算与停止决策提供基准设计线索，但对象是社会意义理解而非 latent 推理，与内部状态的关联尚需核查。
